record.original_question: Under the same definitions of Type-A and Type-B vertex orders for a graph G, if G admits a Type-A order or a Type-B order, can such an order be found in polynomial time?

evidence.quote: Type-A order: for each v in V (G), d-(v) is odd or equal to 0; Type-B order: for each v in V (G), d-(v) is odd or equal to 0 (as in a Type-A order), or d-(v) is even and d+(v) = 0.
Problem 7.2 If a Type-A or Type-B order exists, can it be found in polynomial time?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G = (V, E)$ be a finite simple undirected graph. For a linear order $\pi = (v_1, v_2, \dots, v_n)$ of $V(G)$ and a vertex $v \in V(G)$, define
$$d^-(v) := |\{u \in V(G) : uv \in E(G) \text{ and } u \text{ precedes } v \text{ in } \pi\}|,$$
$$d^+(v) := |\{u \in V(G) : uv \in E(G) \text{ and } v \text{ precedes } u \text{ in } \pi\}|.$$
The order $\pi$ is called:
- a Type-A order if for every $v \in V(G)$, $d^-(v)$ is odd or $d^-(v) = 0$;
- a Type-B order if for every $v \in V(G)$, either $d^-(v)$ is odd, or $d^-(v) = 0$, or $d^-(v)$ is even and $d^+(v) = 0$.

Question: Is there an algorithm that, given as input a graph $G$ that admits a Type-A order (respectively a Type-B order), outputs such an order in time polynomial in $|V(G)| + |E(G)|$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a recently posted (2024) collection of open problems from a workshop on cycles and colourings. No subsequent work resolving the polynomial-time computability of Type-A or Type-B vertex orders was located.

status_evidence.title: Open problems of the 32nd Workshop on Cycles and Colourings
status_evidence.snippet: Collection of open problems including the question of finding Type-A or Type-B vertex orders in polynomial time.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly posed as an open problem (Problem 7.2).
